question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [European power — its primary colonial base in South India during the 18th century]
options: British East India Company — Fort St. George, Madras
French East India Company (Compagnie des Indes) — Pondicherry (Puducherry)
wrong_fact: Masulipatnam (Machilipatnam) was the primary settlement of the British East India Company on the Coromandel Coast before Madras, not of the Dutch. The Dutch (VOC) had their main south Indian settlement at Pulicat (north of Madras), not Masulipatnam.
explanation: The British established their first factory on the Coromandel Coast at Masulipatnam (1611) and later built Fort St. George at Madras (1639). The Dutch VOC's main base in south India was Pulicat (where they established Fort Geldria). Pondicherry was indeed the French headquarters in India, and the Portuguese retained Goa and Daman throughout this period.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Region — dominant colonial power that established supremacy by 1763]
options: Bengal and the Gangetic Plain — British East India Company (after Battle of Plassey, 1757)
Pondicherry and Coromandel Coast — Britain (after the Third Carnatic War, 1763)
Quebec and New France (Canada) — Britain (after the Seven Years' War, 1763)
Caribbean island of Martinique — Britain retained it permanently after 1763
wrong_fact: Martinique was NOT retained permanently by Britain after 1763. Under the Peace of Paris (1763), Martinique was returned to France. Britain chose to retain Canada (New France) rather than Martinique, a decision debated at the time ('Guadeloupe vs Canada' controversy). Martinique remained a French colony.
explanation: After the Seven Years' War, Britain returned Martinique and Guadeloupe to France, preferring to consolidate control over Canada. Bengal came under effective British control after Plassey (1757) and Buxar (1764). Pondicherry was captured and later restored to France but French power in India was broken. Quebec and New France were ceded to Britain permanently.

question: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched? [Colonial outpost — the European nation that founded it and the approximate year of establishment]
options: Pondicherry — French East India Company, founded 1674
Chandernagore (Chandannagar) — French East India Company, established 1692 on the Hooghly River in Bengal
Mahe — French establishment on the Malabar Coast, founded 1725
Karikal — Dutch establishment on the Coromandel Coast, founded 1739
wrong_fact: Karikal (Karaikal) was NOT a Dutch establishment. It was a French settlement on the Coromandel Coast, acquired by the French East India Company in 1739. Along with Pondicherry, Chandernagore, Mahe, and Yanam, Karikal was one of the five French territories (comptoirs) in India.
explanation: The five French territories (Établissements français dans l'Inde) were: Pondicherry (1674), Chandernagore (1692), Mahe (1725), Karikal (1739), and Yanam (1750). The Dutch had no significant settlement called Karikal. Karikal is on the Coromandel Coast, south of Pondicherry, and remained French until 1954.
